annotations.title: Deliver an x402 authorization you signed, and check the chain (paid, x402)

description: PAID: deliver an x402 authorization YOU signed to a seller exactly once, then read the chain for what actually became of it, and get back an immutable receipt of what the seller answered. Read the price to sign with pay_requirements first; we never sign on your behalf. A seller 402, 4xx, 5xx or refused connection is a delivered, billable answer -- what you buy is the truth about what the seller did with your authorization. The receipt is free to re-read with pay_receipt, so a seller who says they were never paid can be shown it. Call it once without payment to receive the price as an x402 PaymentRequired (Base USDC, and Solana USDC where offered); call it again with a signed payment in _meta['x402/payment'] to complete it. The receipt comes back in _meta['x402/payment-response']. No account, no API key. Complaints, questions, quote requests, or a service you wish we had: POST /feedback on this host -- free, no account. Every report is read and analysed daily; there is no individual reply.

authorization.description: The authorization you already signed for the seller. This is NOT the payment that pays us -- that one goes in _meta.

asset.description: The token contract address that authorization was signed against.

header.description: Base64 of the signed x402 PaymentPayload YOU produced for the seller.

headerName.description: X-PAYMENT for a v1 challenge, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for a v2 one.

body.description: Optional request body for the seller.

headers.description: Optional request headers for the seller, at most 20.

method.description: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.

sellerUrl.description: The seller endpoint to deliver the authorization to, an absolute http:// or https:// URL.
